title: A fake repository that keeps the contract
problem: users.py has a UserRepo Protocol, the real SqliteUserRepo and a signup service. Write InMemoryUserRepo in fakes.py so service tests can run without a database. A fake is only useful if it behaves like the real thing: the same contract checks run against both, and the real repository already passes them.
requirements: InMemoryUserRepo has add(email, name) -> int and get_by_email(email) -> dict | None, so it satisfies UserRepo
ids start at 1 and count up; a failed add doesn't use up an id
Email lookups and the duplicate check ignore case, but the stored email keeps its original spelling
A duplicate email (in any case) raises users.DuplicateEmail
get_by_email returns a new dict each time, so callers can't change stored data
contract:
InMemoryUserRepo().add(email: str, name: str) -> int   # raises DuplicateEmail
InMemoryUserRepo().get_by_email(email: str) -> {"id": int, "email": str, "name": str} | None
expectedBehavior: repo.add('Ana@X.io', 'Ana') returns 1; repo.get_by_email('ana@x.io') returns {'id': 1, 'email': 'Ana@X.io', 'name': 'Ana'}; repo.add('ANA@x.io', 'Other') raises DuplicateEmail; the next successful add returns 2.
edgeCases: Lookup with different capitalisation than the stored email
Duplicate that differs only in case
The id counter after a rejected duplicate
Unknown email returns None, not an exception
hints: Conceptual: the real repository is the specification. Read SqliteUserRepo: COLLATE NOCASE means comparisons ignore case, UNIQUE means duplicates fail, and each query builds a fresh dict. Your fake has to reproduce all three.
Specific: keep one dict keyed by email.lower(), storing the user dict with the original email. Check for the key before you hand out an id, so a duplicate doesn't consume one.

Implementation: in add, compute key = email.lower(); if key in the dict, raise DuplicateEmail(email); otherwise take self._next_id, increment it, store {'id': ..., 'email': email, 'name': name}. In get_by_email, return dict(stored) or None.
evaluation: All 9 tests pass, and test_contract_matches_the_real_repo still passes (the checks describe the real behaviour)
No inheritance from UserRepo is needed: it matches structurally
The fake stays small: no SQL parsing, no features the real repository doesn't have
